newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares fall sharply in early bourse trade.
newsitem.headline: German shares fall sharply in early bourse trade.

text.p: German shares fell two percent in early bourse trade as the DAX index catches up on losses made in late trade on Friday. Dealers said volumes were low and sentiment unsettled by the speed of Friday's fall.
"On Friday everyone saw just how quickly the market can go down," said a Frankfurt trader.
The IBIS DAX index fell over one percent in late computer dealings on Friday, but clawed back some of the losses in early electronic trade on Monday.
However, the DAX index opened sharply lower. The DAX was down 88.11 points, or two percent, at 4,320.68 points within the first hour of dealings.
"Everyone is watching to see what everyone else does -- which means that no-one does anything," a trader said, adding that the chances of the market rising at the rate seen in recent weeks were slim.
"We won't see market hikes like we saw on Friday - I don't think we will be able to make up the ground lost. Everyone is unsettled, worried about interest rates," the trader said.
Some support for the market came from the dollar's strength at 1.86 marks, which has been behind much of the market's rise in recent months as it boosts German exports.
Blue-chip losses were down across the board.
Chemical giant BASF AG was down 55 pfennigs at 70.10 marks and Bayer was down 85 pfennigs at 75.65 marks, while pharmaceutical group Schering AG was down 2.70 marks at 200 marks.
Airline Deutsche Lufthansa AG was down 90 pfennigs at 35.40 marks.

Again banks were in the spotlight as merger speculation in the sector continued. Bankgesellschaft Berlin was up 20 pfennigs at 46.30 marks during floor trade, having earlier risen in pre-bourse trade.
Bayerische Hypo-Bank, soon to merger with fellow Bavarian bank Vereinsbank was among the chief losers in floor trade, down 4.15 percent at 72.80 marks.
